thread.title: US STOCKS-Amazon jitters offset upbeat jobs data on Wall Street By Reuters

author: Reuters
title: US STOCKS-Amazon jitters offset upbeat jobs data on Wall Street By Reuters
text:
© Reuters. US STOCKS-Amazon jitters offset upbeat jobs data on Wall Street * Amazon drops over 5 pct after sales forecast misses estimates
* January U.S. payrolls rise more than expected
* Oil prices, strong earnings boost energy sector
* Dow up 0.26 pct, S&P 500 up 0.09 pct, Nasdaq down 0.25 pct (Updates to close)
By Noel Randewich
Feb 1 (Reuters) - Wall Street ended mixed on Friday, as optimism from a surge in January U.S. job growth was offset by a weaker-than-expected outlook from Amazon.com Inc AMZN.O that battered retail stocks.
The online retail heavyweight slumped 5.38 percent after its quarterly sales forecast fell short of Wall Street estimates, overshadowing its record sales and profit during the holiday season. results put the Nasdaq in negative territory, while retailers Walmart (NYSE: WMT ) Inc WMT.N , Macy's Inc M.N and Kohl's Corp KSS.N each dropped more than 2 percent. The S&P consumer discretionary index .SPLRCD fell 1.77 percent.
A U.S. Labor Department report showed nonfarm payrolls jumped by 304,000 jobs last month, the largest gain since February 2018 and beating economists' expectations for an increase of 165,000. report, along with better-than-expected ISM manufacturing activity numbers for January, pointed to underlying strength in the economy despite an uncertain outlook that has left the Federal Reserve wary about more U.S. interest rate hikes this year.
"What the unemployment report is telling you is that people want to go back to work," said Tom Martin, senior portfolio manager at GlobAlt Investments in Atlanta. "The consumer needs to be strong, and if the consumer is employed, the consumer will stay strong."
Even as the U.S. economy remains on a stable footing, investors are concerned that a slowdown overseas could hurt profit growth, with high-profile companies such as Apple Inc AAPL.O warning of slower demand in China.
Data showed China's manufacturing sector shrank in January for the second straight month, heightening risks for global growth amid a trade war with United States. Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI climbed 0.26 percent to end the week at 25,063.89 points, while the S&P 500 .SPX edged 0.09 percent higher to 2,706.53.
The Nasdaq Composite .IXIC dropped 0.25 percent to 7,263.87.
The S&P 500 rose 1.6 percent for the week and the benchmark index is up 8 percent so far in 2019, but it still remains 8 percent below its record high close on Sept. 20, 2018.
The Dow added 1.3 percent for the week and the Nasdaq gained 1.4 percent.
During Friday's session, Exxon Mobil Corp (NYSE: XOM ) XOM.N and Chevron Corp (NYSE: CVX ) CVX.N jumped more than 3 percent apiece after the oil majors reported better-than-expected quarterly profits, boosting the Dow Jones Industrials. S&P energy index .SPNY rallied 1.83 percent, also helped by higher oil prices.
Cigna Corp (NYSE: CI ) CI.N slid 2.88 percent lower after the health insurer forecast 2019 revenue and earnings below estimates. issues outnumbered declining ones on the NYSE by a 1.30-to-1 ratio; on Nasdaq, a 1.37-to-1 ratio favored advancers.
The S&P 500 posted 29 new 52-week highs and no new lows; the Nasdaq Composite recorded 51 new highs and 20 new lows.
Volume on U.S. exchanges was 7.5 billion shares, compared with the 7.7 billion share average over the last 20 trading days.
